items.title: Five-year risk of cardiovascular events in women with history of pregnancy complicated by fetal growth restriction.
items.abstract: To evaluate the association between fetal growth restriction (FGR) and adverse maternal cardiovascular outcomes within 5 years postpartum. This was a retrospective study that used a global federated health research network (TriNetX) in which diagnoses are coded using the International Classification of Diseases, tenth revision, Clinical Modification system (ICD-10-CM). Nulliparous women aged ≥ 18 years, without prior cardiovascular disease and with a singleton pregnancy delivered between April 2006 and December 2020, were categorized by the presence or absence of FGR (ICD-10-CM: O36.5). 1:1 propensity-score matching (PSM) was applied using two models: Model 1, matching for pre-existing cardiovascular risk factors; and Model 2, matching for both pre-existing and other pregnancy-related cardiovascular risk factors. Cox regression proportional hazard models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% CI for a maternal composite cardiovascular outcome including heart failure, acute myocardial infarction and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke within 5 years postpartum, and for each of these components individually. After PSM, 84 863 women per group were analyzed in Model 1 and 84 861 per group in Model 2. FGR was associated with an increased risk of the composite cardiovascular outcome (Model 1: HR, 1.33 (95% CI, 1.16-1.52); Model 2: HR, 1.31 (95% CI, 1.15-1.50)), as well as with an increased risk of each of the components of the composite outcome individually: heart failure (Model 1: HR, 1.29 (95% CI, 1.08-1.54); Model 2: HR, 1.30 (95% CI, 1.09-1.56)), acute myocardial infarction (Model 1: HR, 1.55 (95% CI, 1.16-2.08); Model 2: HR, 1.53 (95% CI, 1.15-2.05)) and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke (Model 1: HR, 1.38 (95% CI, 1.09-1.74); Model 2: HR, 1.33 (95% CI, 1.06-1.68)) within 5 years postpartum. FGR in a first pregnancy is associated with increased maternal composite cardiovascular risk, including heart failure, acute myocardial infarction and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke, within 5 years postpartum. These findings suggest that FGR may be a marker of early cardiovascular vulnerability. However, residual confounding, particularly by unmeasured timing or severity of pre-eclampsia, cannot be excluded. Also, FGR was identified using coding constructs based on electronic health records, which may include overlap with broader 'suspected poor growth' phenotypes such as small-for-gestational age, hence potentially diluting the observed associations. Earlier risk assessment and preventive strategies may help to reduce the risk of long-term morbidity and mortality in this population. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Statins for the Prevention of Dementia Among Older Male United States Veterans: A Target Trial Emulation.
items.abstract: Several observational studies have reported a lower risk of dementia in statin users compared with nonusers, but these findings may be susceptible to bias. Whether statins prevent dementia would ideally be studied in a large, randomized trial that includes older adults followed for a long follow-up period. In the absence of such a trial, we can explicitly emulate a target trial of statins and risk of dementia using observational data. Using electronic health records from the US Department of Veterans Affairs, we emulated a target trial of statin therapy and 10-year risk of dementia. Eligible individuals were men aged 60 years or older with no history of dementia, cardiovascular disease, chronic renal disease, diabetes, or statin use in the past year. The treatment strategies to be compared were initiation of any statin and continuation over follow-up (until the development of a contraindication or serious health condition) vs no statin initiation. The outcome of interest was diagnosis of any dementia. Risks were estimated through a pooled logistic regression model adjusted for baseline and time-varying covariates. A total of 81,599 statin initiators and 843,615 noninitiators were eligible for this study. The median age (interquartile range) was 64.3 years (61.2-70.3), and 11.7% were Black. The estimated 10-year dementia risks were 9.4% (95% CI 8.5-9.9) for statins and 9.6% (95% CI 8.9-10.3) for no statins. The corresponding risk difference was -0.2% (95% CI -0.9 to 0.4), and the risk ratio was 0.98 (95% CI 0.89-1.15). Estimates were similar within subgroups defined at baseline according to age, race, and frailty status based on deficit accumulation. Although the possibility of unmeasured confounding or misclassification cannot be entirely excluded, as in any observational study, this study involving a nationwide cohort of older male US veterans without prior cardiovascular disease suggests that statin therapy does not meaningfully influence dementia incidence over 10 years. Per American Academy of Neurology Class of Evidence Classification, this study provides Class III evidence that statins do not reduce the incidence of dementia in men aged 60 years or older.

items.title: The Combined Effect of Migraine and Smoking on Premature Stroke and All-Cause Mortality in Parous Women: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
items.abstract: Migraine and smoking are established stroke risk factors. We examined the individual and combined effects of migraine and smoking on risk of premature stroke (age 60 years or younger) and all-cause mortality in women and evaluated additive interaction. We conducted a population-based cohort study using nationwide Danish health registries (1996-2022). Women aged 15-60 years giving birth during 1996-2022 were identified through the Danish Medical Birth Registry and categorized as having migraine, smoking, both exposures, or neither (reference). Participants were followed until stroke, death, emigration, 61st birthday, or December 31, 2022. Outcomes were ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and all-cause mortality. Absolute risks (ARs), adjusted hazard ratios (HRs), and relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) were estimated. Among 1,677,707 women (median age 29-32 years across exposure groups), the 20-year AR of premature ischemic stroke was 0.8% in the reference cohort (n = 1,389,361), 1.3% with migraine (n = 65,422), 1.5% with smoking (n = 214,277), and 2.8% with both exposures (n = 8,647). ARs of premature hemorrhagic stroke were 0.3%, 0.5%, 0.6%, and 0.9%. All-cause mortality ARs were 1.0%, 1.2%, 2.3%, and 3.4%. Compared with the reference cohort, adjusted HRs for premature ischemic stroke were 1.85 (95% CI 1.66-2.05) for migraine, 2.10 (95% CI 1.99-2.20) for smoking, and 3.61 (95% CI 3.03-4.31) for both exposures. HRs for premature hemorrhagic stroke were 1.46 (95% CI 1.23-1.74), 2.02 (95% CI 1.87-2.18), and 2.60 (95% CI 1.91-3.54). For all-cause mortality, HRs were 1.08 (95% CI 0.96-1.22), 2.44 (95% CI 2.34-2.54), and 3.30 (95% CI 2.80-3.88). The 20-year RERI was 0.67 (95% CI 0.22-1.13) for ischemic stroke, 0.11 (95% CI -0.59-0.82) for hemorrhagic stroke, and 0.78 (95% CI 0.34-1.22) for mortality. Migraine and smoking were associated with elevated risk of premature stroke, and mortality risk was increased among women who smoked regardless of migraine status. Additive interaction indicated excess risk of ischemic stroke and all-cause mortality among women with migraine who smoked. These findings support targeted cessation strategies to reduce premature vascular events and mortality.

items.title: Flavonoid Intake Diversity, Metabolic Signatures, and Risk of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
items.abstract: Higher flavonoid intake has been associated with a lower risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, flavonoids vary substantially in chemical structure, bioavailability, and metabolism. Therefore, whether greater diversity in flavonoid intake confers additional protection against COPD remains unclear. To investigate the association between flavonoid intake diversity and incident COPD and to explore potential metabolic mediators underlying this association. This prospective study included 93,068 participants from the UK Biobank. Flavonoid intake was estimated from 24-h dietary assessments, and intake diversity was quantified using the Shannon entropy and Hill number indices. Elastic net regression was applied to derive metabolic signatures associated with flavonoid intake diversity, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations of flavonoid intake diversity and its metabolic signature with incident COPD. Greater diversity of dietary flavonoids was associated with a lower risk of incident COPD independent of total intake. Participants in the highest quintile of flavonoid intake diversity had a 27% lower COPD risk than those in the lowest quintile (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.62, 0.85). Similar associations were observed across flavonoid subclasses. In joint analyses, the lowest risk was observed among participants with both moderate-to-high flavonoid intake and high diversity. The diversity-related metabolic signature was also inversely associated with COPD risk (HR for Q5 vs Q1: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.70). This signature significantly mediated the association between flavonoid intake diversity and COPD risk, primarily through pathways related to lipid and amino acid metabolism, inflammation, and fluid homeostasis. Greater diversity in flavonoid intake was associated with a lower risk of COPD and may operate through multiple metabolic pathways. These findings support flavonoid intake diversity as a potentially modifiable dietary factor for COPD prevention.

items.title: MYCN amplification suppresses PD-L1 and CXCL10 to drive an immunosuppressive microenvironment in neuroblastoma.
items.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Qiao et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most common extracranial solid tumor in children, and outcomes for patients with high-risk disease remain poor despite intensive multimodal therapy. MYCN amplification is associated with unfavorable prognosis and an immunologically “cold” tumor microenvironment (TME). This study investigated the impact of MYCN amplification on the expression of PD-L1 and the chemokine CXCL10, two important regulators of antitumor immunity. Analysis of NB patient datasets revealed that MYCN amplification was associated with reduced expression of both PD-L1 and CXCL10. Higher expression of PD-L1 and CXCL10 correlated with significantly improved overall survival. In contrast, PD-1 and PD-L2 showed weaker associations with MYCN status and were not linked to survival outcomes. In MYCN amplified NB cell lines, PD-L1 expression remained inducible by interferon-γ (IFNγ). Silencing MYCN further enhanced IFNγ-induced PD-L1 expression at both mRNA and protein levels, indicating that MYCN suppresses PD-L1 responsiveness. The BET inhibitor JQ1 reduced IFNγ-induced PD-L1 expression regardless of MYCN status, whereas inhibition of CXCL10 secretion was observed only in MYCN non-amplified cells. Retinoic acid (RA), a standard component of NB therapy, increased PD-L1 mRNA expression in all cell lines but increased PD-L1 protein expression primarily in MYCN non-amplified cells. Overall, these findings identify MYCN as a key regulator of immune signaling in NB and suggest that MYCN amplification contributes to an immune-cold tumor phenotype through suppression of PD-L1 and CXCL10 expression. MYCN status may therefore serve as a biomarker for immune stratification and guide the development of combination immunotherapeutic strategies for high-risk NB.

items.title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy.
items.abstract: Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFY p HH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFY p HH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a trans -cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFY p HH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

items.title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment.
items.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition-associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type-specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type-enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

items.title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy via hypoxia aggravation for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy.
items.abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

items.title: Targeting cancer immune evasion with anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate potentiates anti-PD-1 efficacy in colorectal cancer.
items.abstract: Loss of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) antigen presentation in tumor cells drives immune evasion and resistance to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in colorectal cancer (CRC). To identify therapeutic targets reversing this, we conducted fluorescence-activated cell sorting-based CRISPR activation screens using a druggable genome library and identified folate receptor α (FOLR1) as a top negative regulator. FOLR1 was heterogeneously expressed in CRC tumors but undetectable in adjacent normal tissues. High expression of FOLR1 predicted a poor ICB response, enhanced cancer stemness, and unfavorable patient outcomes. Functional assays showed that FOLR1 promoted CRC stemness-associated properties and fostered an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) with impaired CD8 + T cell infiltration and cytotoxicity, thereby driving tumor progression. Proteomic analyses revealed that FOLR1 stabilized the lactyltransferase AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1), which lactylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) at lysine-193 (K193), facilitating its interaction with TCPTP (T cell protein-tyrosine phosphatase) and inducing STAT1 dephosphorylation at tyrosine-701. Consequently, impaired STAT1 signaling down-regulated MHC-I and up-regulated MYC proto-oncogene protein (c-MYC), facilitating evasion of T cell surveillance and enhancing cancer stemness. The anti-FOLR1 antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) mirvetuximab soravtansine (IMGN853) exhibited potent activity against FOLR1-positive CRC cells, reprogramming the TME to an immune-active status. Combining IMGN853 with anti-PD-1 (programmed cell death protein-1) therapy boosted antitumor immunity, sensitized tumors to immunotherapy, and induced robust tumor regression in vivo. Our findings support anti-FOLR1 ADC as a clinically actionable approach to overcome immune evasion and unlock immunotherapy efficacy in CRC.

items.title: Cluster analysis of high-cost patients in Japan: A longitudinal study using health insurance data.
items.abstract: This study aimed to identify distinct patterns of medical expenditure trajectories among high-cost patients in Japan and characterise the identified groups using diagnostic and health check-up data, including laboratory test results. This retrospective study analysed data from 190,190 high-cost patients (top 5% of annual medical expenditure in fiscal year 2021) in the Japanese JMDC Claims Database. Five-year healthcare expenditure trajectories were classified using K-means clustering. The resulting clusters were characterised according to demographic characteristics, disease patterns, hospitalisation rates, and health check-up data. Eighteen clusters were identified and further grouped into four descriptive types of expenditure trajectory. The 'over-30-million-yen (200,000 USD)' type included two clusters with rare, high-cost diseases such as haematological disorders, chronic viral hepatitis, and sphingolipid metabolism disorders. The 'flat' type (four clusters) showed relatively smooth expenditure patterns over time, associated with chronic conditions like dialysis and secondary cancers. In contrast, the 'gradual peak' type exhibited costs that increased over time, largely due to malignant neoplasms. Meanwhile, the 'sharp peak' type was characterised by sudden cost surges driven primarily by inpatient care, with a high prevalence of angina and atrial fibrillation. By analysing five-year expenditure trajectories at the individual level, this study identified distinct longitudinal patterns and provided a descriptive framework for understanding heterogeneity among high-cost patients.

items.title: Clinical characteristics, temporal trends, and predictors of liver transplantation-free survival in patients with autoimmune hepatitis: a nationwide Japanese registry study.
items.abstract: Complete biochemical response (CBR) is a key therapeutic target in autoimmune hepatitis (AIH), but nationwide Japanese data linking treatment response, temporal changes in practice, and liver transplantation (LT)-free survival remain limited. We evaluated clinical characteristics, diagnostic period trends, and predictors of LT-free survival using the Japanese Autoimmune Hepatitis Study Group registry. Patients newly diagnosed with AIH between 1998 and 2024 were screened. Baseline diagnostic data were available for 3992 patients, and 2494 patients with follow-up data were included in the survival analysis. Landmark analyses were performed at 6 and 12 months after treatment initiation. CBR was defined as the normalization of serum AST, ALT, and IgG levels. LT-free survival was assessed using Kaplan‒Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. Among 3992 patients, 1163 were diagnosed from 2018 onward. Recent patients were older and had a slightly lower female proportion, more frequent cirrhosis at diagnosis, and more frequent azathioprine and ursodeoxycholic acid use. In the survival cohort, the median age was 63 years, 82.6% were female, and 10.8% had cirrhosis. During a median follow-up of 3.2 years, CBR was achieved in 53.5% at the 6-month landmark and 66.9% at the 12-month landmark. The estimated LT-free survival rates were 96.6% at 3 years and 95.8% at 5 years. Older age, male sex, cirrhosis at diagnosis, and a lack of CBR at the 6- or 12-month landmark independently predicted poorer LT-free survival. In liver-specific analyses, cirrhosis at diagnosis and lack of early CBR remained associated with liver-related death or LT. Baseline cirrhosis and failure to achieve early CBR may help identify high-risk AIH patients who require closer monitoring and clinical reassessment.

items.title: Hepatitis B splicing-generated protein prevents tumor initiation but shapes a pro-tumor immune microenvironment in established HCC.
items.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) plays a key role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through both direct oncogenic and indirect immune-mediated mechanisms. Expression of the main HBV spliced transcript, sp1RNA, gradually increases in chronic carriers prior to HCC onset. However, sp1RNA and related Hepatitis B Splicing-generated Protein (HBSP) contributions to hepatic carcinogenesis and tumor microenvironment have not been investigated. HBV-related HCC tumors from 57 patients were classified according to HBV expression (RT)-qPCR and profiled using Nanostring immuno-oncology panel. The functional impact of HBSP expression was evaluated in transgenic male mice (TgHBSP) subjected to diethylnitrosamine (DEN)-induced HCC. A second model using orthotopic allografts of HBSP-expressing cells was developed. Liver tissues and immune infiltrates were characterized at 48 h, 6- and 10-month post-DEN injection. In HBV-related HCC patients, sp1RNA expression was associated with worse overall survival and reduced monocyte/macrophage gene signature within tumors. In TgHBSP mice, tumor incidence was reduced at both 6- and 10-month post-DEN administration, associated with sustained p38-MAPK activation at the initiation stage of cancer. Despite lower tumor incidence, tumors arising in TgHBSP mice were twice as large at endpoint. Attenuated inflammatory signaling and macrophage polarization towards a pro-tumor phenotype were implicated in the pro-tumor effect of HBSP at early HCC. This study reveals a dual, stage-dependent, role for HBSP in liver carcinogenesis, exerting first anti-tumor effects associated with p38-MAPK activation at initiation stage of hepatic cancer, then pro-tumor effect on tumor growth and alterations in the immune microenvironment of established HCC.

items.title: The Association of Oral and Anogenital Human Papillomavirus Genotypes With Head and Neck Cancers in Brazil: A Nationwide Case-Control Study.
items.abstract: This multicenter case-control study assessed (2019-2023) the association of oral and anogenital human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes with head and neck cancers in Brazil. Eligible cases were adults (≥ 18 years) with newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, or larynx. Controls (cancer-free individuals) were matched a posteriori by region, sex, and age. Oral, genital, and anal samples were collected and processed at a central laboratory for HPV genotyping. Associations were estimated using conditional regression. Analyses included 314 participants (157 cases, 157 controls), mostly males (79%) aged 50-65 years (51%). Oral HPV prevalence was similar between cases and controls (14% vs. 12%), predominantly involving high-risk genotypes (35 out of 40); HPV-16/18 was more prevalent among cases (7.3% vs. 1.9%; p = 0.024), with most HPV-16/18-positive cancers located in the oropharynx (10 out of 11). Genital HPV prevalence was 39% with no case-control differences, while anal HPV prevalence was 17%. Cases were more frequently positive for any high-risk anal HPV type than controls (16% vs. 9%; p = 0.049). Minimal genotype concordance was observed between oral and anogenital sites. Current smokers had ten-fold higher odds of being cases (adjustedOR 10.0; 95% CI 2.92-34.6). Oral HPV-16/18 infection was independently associated with head and neck cancer (adjustedOR 6.30; 95% CI 1.52-26.1). Multisite HPV genotyping revealed site-specific colonization patterns, with genital infections being most prevalent among both men and women. After multivariable adjustment, only oral HPV-16/18 infection was strongly associated with head and neck cancer, especially oropharyngeal carcinoma.

items.title: Rescue of glutaric aciduria type I by GalNAc-conjugated siRNA against aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase.
items.abstract: Glutaric aciduria type I (GA-1) is a severe metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency of glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenase (GCDH), leading to accumulation of organic acids in the brain and resulting in striatal injury and progressive movement disorders. Although early diagnosis and dietary management reduce risk, one-third of patients still develop debilitating neurological complications. We previously demonstrated that liver-specific deletion of aminoadipate semialdehyde synthase (AASS), an upstream enzyme in lysine degradation, is a promising therapeutic strategy. Here, we tested an N -acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated siRNA against Aass . Treatment of neonatal Gcdh -/- mice rescued lethality and improved the brain pathology while reducing toxic metabolites in the brain and other organs. Serum biomarkers, including glutaric acid, 3-hydroxyglutaric acid, and glutarylcarnitine, predicted neurological outcomes, supporting their use for therapeutic monitoring. Although systemic metabolite concentrations declined, their urinary excretion remained elevated, consistent with a renal washout phenomenon and preserved excretory capacity. These findings demonstrate the potential of liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapy as a treatment for GA-1.

items.title: Kluyveromyces marxianus CIDCA 8154 Attenuates Intestinal Damage in a Murine Model of Irinotecan Induced Mucositis Without Affecting Anti-Tumor Efficacy.
items.abstract: Intestinal mucositis is a common and severe side effect of cancer chemotherapy that continues to have a detrimental impact on patients' quality of life and treatment outcomes. Irinotecan is one of the chemotherapeutic drugs most frequently associated to this condition. Therefore, the development of new strategies to prevent or reduce mucositis remains a clinical need. Probiotics have been suggested as potential candidates for mucositis prevention and some bacterial strains have shown a protective effect.In this study, we evaluate the effect of the probiotic yeast Kluyveromyces marxianus CIDCA 8154 in a murine model of irinotecan induced intestinal mucositis. Administration of K. marxianus 8154 significantly improved clinical symptoms, reducing body weight loss and diarrhea development. In addition, it preserved gut mucosal integrity, attenuating villus shortening, crypt hyperplasia and decreasing the proportion of crypts containing proliferating cells. Mice receiving K. marxianus 8154 also showed decreased gut myeloperoxidase activity and eosinophilic infiltrate suggesting a reduced inflammatory injury. In vitro, K. marxianus 8154 reduced intestinal epithelial inflammatory response induced by irinotecan decreasing activation of Caco-2 ccl20-luciferase reporter cells and IL-8 secretion. Moreover, probiotic treatment mitigated irinotecan-induced oxidative stress, by reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in liver and gut, while preserving at basal levels irinotecan induced activation of the antioxidant master regulator Nrf2. Importantly, treatment with K. marxianus 8154 did not impair the ability of irinotecan to control CT-26 cell-derived tumor growth. These findings suggest that K. marxianus 8154 has a protective role on irinotecan induced intestinal mucositis without impairing its anti-tumoral activity.

items.title: PES1 promotes hepatocellular carcinoma growth by triggering CDK7/MDK-dependent neutrophil extracellular trap formation.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by a high recurrence rate and poor prognosis, requiring the identification of novel molecular drivers within the tumor-immune microenvironment. In this study, by performing a targeted prognostic prioritization of the HCC transcriptome via median survival and hazard ratio modeling, pescadillo ribosomal biogenesis factor 1 (PES1) was identified as a key prognostic driver, validated through survival intervals and tissue expression. While PES1 is a known component of the PeBoW complex involved in cell cycle regulation, its role in modulating the HCC immune microenvironment remains undefined. Netx, we performed a secondary screening across various leukocyte lineages using conditioned medium from PES1-overexpressing HCC cells. This functional screening revealed that PES1 specifically triggers the expression of elastase, a key functional component of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), with predominant effects on neutrophils. Driven by this targeted induction of a NET-associated marker, we subsequently quantified MPO-DNA complexes and confirmed that PES1 indeed promotes the formation of NETs. In vivo, the PES1-driven acceleration of tumor growth was effectively abrogated by degradation of NET-DNA using DNase I, demonstrating that PES1-mediated malignancy is NET-dependent. Mechanistically, we identified midkine (MDK) as the primary effector significantly upregulated and secreted by PES1-overexpressing HCC cells. Neutralization of MDK signaling via iMDK effectively abolished PES1-induced NET formation. Furthermore, we demonstrated that CDK7 suppression inhibited PES1-driven MDK upregulation. This dependency was further validated that THZ1-mediated inhibition of CDK7 effectively abolished both MDK secretion and subsequent NET formation. This PES1/CDK7/MDK axis triggers NET formation by activating peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4), a process that could be targeted via pharmacological inhibition of PAD4 to suppress the pro-tumorigenic niche. Taken together, these findings identify the PES1/CDK7/MDK/PAD4 axis as a critical driver of NET-mediated HCC progression, underscoring the potential value of PES1 as a prognostic biomarker and a therapeutic target in HCC.
